claim.pdf_says: Two full columns of index entries, from "WRITE statement" through "== pseudo-text delimiter, III-18, IV-42" (page XVIII-13)
claim.why_it_matters: The whole body of index page XVIII-13 is absent: the markdown keeps only the running header and folio. Every index entry (term to page references) printed on this page is lost, so the transcription's index section is empty for this page. The index is not normative, but it is content the page prints.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 819 (folio XVIII-13) shows ONE column (not two) of index entries from 'WRITE statement' through '== pseudo-text delimiter, III-18, IV-42', and the markdown's Page 819 section holds only 'Index' and 'XVIII-13'. But the omission is a deliberate, recorded amendment application, not a transcription loss: under '## Page 807' the transcription carries Errata C337, which applies Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993, page 960, folio B-48): 'Replace the index on pages XVIII-1 through XVIII-13 with the index on pages B-49 through B-64'; it states the base index's entries are deleted from pages 807 to 819, each keeping its running header and folio, and the replacement is held once at PDF pages 961-976. The same entries printed on page 819 appear verbatim in the markdown under '## Page 976' (lines ~36283-36326: 'WRITE statement / Conditional statement, IV-37 ... == pseudo-text delimiter, III-18, IV-42'), and I confirmed page 976 (folio B-64) prints them. The departure is listed in the Errata with printed form, page and source, per the transcription's stated policy, so nothing is lost and there is no unrecorded discrepancy. The claim also misdescribes the page as two columns.
